label: the wrench (models/v_crowbar.mdl, models/p_crowbar.mdl, models/w_crowbar.mdl): a pipe wrench: red-painted handle worn to bare iron, a heavy toothed jaw

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_crowbar.mdl, models/w_357.mdl, models/w_satchel.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, C, B, D where the asset was D, B, D, A: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The brief asks for a pipe wrench: a long handle ending in an open, toothed jaw. In sides.png the head is a closed, boxy block about half the length of the piece (top, below and front-left views). The jaw has no gap or mouth, and the teeth sit on the block's outer faces. The handle is short and stubby beside the head. The outline reads as a club or hammer-head more than a pipe wrench.

M2.reason: Measured length is 20.2 against the brief's 18, which is 12.5% off and inside the 15% line. Width 5.5 and height 15.4 are not asked for by the brief.

M3.reason: The parts the brief names are all there: the red-painted handle with bare iron showing at the head end and tip (sides.png right and back-right views, first-person.png), and the toothed jaw, with small silver teeth along both jaw edges in the top and below views and in in-hand.png. The teeth are small and few, but present. No brief-named part is missing, and the lineup's Valve models show no jaw or adjuster part to hold it to.

M4.reason: The handle is red paint as briefed, and the head is iron grey-brown, with silver where the iron shows. Each region has a plausible colour and material in lineup.png and sides.png.

M5.reason: The wear the brief asks for is only a silver cap at each end of the handle (sides.png, top and front-right views). The rest of the red handle reads as unworn paint, with no scuffs or bare-iron patches along it. The teeth are fine and the head has few panel marks, so the detail is thinner than the brief describes.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric. The line-up test (lineup.png, D among A to D) was caught once in four readings, so it was not picked twice or more.

M7.reason: The w_ model lies flat on its back in sides.png, with the handle and head in one plane along the long axis, which is how a dropped tool rests. Nothing sinks below the floor or floats above it. The brief names no front, so there is nothing further to check.

M8.reason: Measured at 152 triangles, under the cap of 284 (twice the Half-Life median of 142). Nothing is open or inside out in any view. The handle sits on the head in back-left and front-right, and the teeth plates touch the head in below and front-left.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the wrench sits lower and further right than the game's crowbar, which is fully in view. Its head is cut by the view's bottom and right edges, and its handle runs out at the top right. Its head points down and its handle rises, where the crowbar's hook points up. The attack frames (attack.png) show it leaving the picture at frames 1 to 3, but no hands are shown there, so no parting is charged. The placement and orientation are the fault.
